p: popular by the early 7th century; ongoing
d: Desert falconry with saker falcons, using the blocked burqa hood with pleated back, the mangalah cuff and flat-topped block perches.
tech: hand-stitched blocked leather hoods
mat: leather

p: Late Muromachi period (16th century) to present
d: Japanese incense-appreciation tradition whose utensils, incense woods and boxes are collected as objects; the practice itself belongs to the pursuit taxonomy.
tech: Agarwood slivers heated on a mica plate over ash in a censer; incense-guessing games
mat: Kyara and jinkō agarwood, sandalwood, aromatics
auth: Wood grade and origin of the agarwood; school-specific utensils such as the Shino incense packet

r: Arabian Peninsula, Gulf and wider Muslim world
d: Burning scented chips, pastilles and agarwood in a mabkhara to perfume homes and welcome guests.
tech: Indirect burning on charcoal in a censer
mat: Agarwood (oud), bakhoor paste, resins
auth: Real agarwood is dense, dark and resinous; adulteration and plantation wood are common

d: Stickless herbal incense from monastery and Tibetan-medicine formulas.
tech: Extruded into lengths or coils, no bamboo core
mat: Himalayan herbs, often 30 or more ingredients
auth: Traceable lineage to a monastery or medical college; authentic Himalayan herbs

p: Ancient; bamboo-core stick from the late 19th century
d: Indian stick incense made from a paste on bamboo, scented with masala or perfume oils.
tech: Hand-rolled masala paste on bamboo; dhoop rolled or extruded without a core
mat: Charcoal or sawdust, jiggit binder, halmaddi resin, sandalwood
auth: Hand-rolled masala texture versus dipped charcoal sticks

d: China's main centre of firework and firecracker making for over 1,400 years, exporting since 1875.
tech: hand and factory filling of paper-cased crackers and shells
mat: black powder, paper, clay
auth: Liuyang fireworks are a protected origin product

d: Kiln production of hard white charcoal from ubame oak, designated an intangible folk cultural property of Wakayama in 1974.
tech: Slow kiln pyrolysis (about 240 °C for 120 hours), final firing near 1,000 °C, then smothering in damp earth, sand and ash
mat: Ubame oak (Quercus phillyreoides)
auth: Yellow label of the Wakayama Prefectural Charcoal Cooperative; Regional Collective Trademark (2006); metallic ring when struck

d: Hot-air bathing at 80–110 °C with löyly from water on the stones of a kiuas, alternated with cooling off.
tech: wood or electric stove with stones; löyly; birch whisking
mat: wood, stone, birch
auth: wood stove with stone mass; sessions with vihta/vasta whisk

d: Chimneyless smoke sauna tradition including bathing customs, whisk-making, sauna building and meat smoking.
tech: stone-covered stove without chimney; smoke vented before bathing
mat: wood, stone
auth: no chimney; raised platform; smoke-blackened interior

d: Wood-heated steam bath with venik whisking, in black (smoke) or white (piped) form.
tech: stove with firebox, stone chamber and water tank; venik
mat: wood, stone, birch, oak
auth: three-room plan; venik; felt hat

p: Umayyad period onwards; classical peak 16th century
d: Steam bath descended from Roman thermae, with warm and hot rooms and a heated marble navel stone.
tech: furnace and hypocaust; steam
mat: marble, plaster
auth: marble göbek taşı; domed hot room with skylights

d: Deep, square soaking bath entered after washing, traditionally wooden (hinoki) or a wood-fired cast-iron goemon-buro.
tech: soak at 38–42 °C after rinsing; wood-fired kettle in goemon-buro
mat: hinoki wood, cast iron
auth: deep square tub; no overflow; hinoki wood

n: Henna: rituals, aesthetic and social practices
r: Arab states and North Africa (UAE, Algeria, Bahrain, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Mauritania, Morocco, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sudan, Tunisia, Yemen)
p: ancient to present; UNESCO Representative List 2024
d: Henna body art and rites such as the Night of the Henna, inscribed by UNESCO on a 16-state nomination.
tech: leaf powder mixed to a paste, applied by stick or syringe, left to stain
mat: Lawsonia inermis leaves
auth: Real henna stains reddish-brown and darkens over a day or two; 'black henna' that stains black fast contains PPD and can cause severe allergy and scarring.

d: South Asian henna art on hands, wrists, forearms and feet for weddings, religious festivals and family ceremonies.
tech: paste piped from a plastic cone, brush or stick; dries, cracks and is left to stain
mat: henna powder, water or lemon, oils
auth: Body-art-quality henna is finely sifted; avoid PPD 'black henna' (Florida Department of Health, FDA warnings).

r: Egypt, Middle East, North and West Africa
d: Mineral eye cosmetic worn by Egyptians of all classes and spread through Arabia, North Africa and West Africa.
tech: crushing mineral to fine powder; applied with a stick
mat: stibnite (antimony sulfide); modern often galena (lead sulfide), charcoal
ctr: Hausa, Fulani, Tuareg and Yoruba peoples
auth: Many traditional kohls contain lead; the FDA warns against kohl, kajal, al-kahal, surma, tiro, tozali and kwalli for lead poisoning risk.

d: Soot-based kajal and mineral surma worn by women and children, also against the evil eye and in classical dance.
tech: kajal: soot from burning oil or ghee mixed with oil; surma: ground mineral
mat: soot, ghee, camphor, sandalwood; galena or other minerals
auth: Both have been linked to chemical toxicity, especially lead; prefer products with ingredient lists.

d: Red powders marking marital status in the hair parting (sindoor) and worn as forehead marks (kumkum).
tech: turmeric dried and powdered with slaked lime, alum or lime turns it red
mat: turmeric, alum, slaked lime; historically vermilion or red lead
auth: Herbal turmeric-based powder is non-toxic; some commercial sindoor contains lead (FDA warning on Swad sindoor).

r: India, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and diaspora
d: Forehead dot worn by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists, red or maroon after sindoor and kumkum, now often a sticker.
tech: painted with powder, or self-adhesive felt or metal
mat: kumkum, sindoor, lac, felt, thin metal
auth: Traditional bindi is painted; lac tikli preceded modern stickers.

d: Traditional extraction of argan oil, mostly by rural women, for food, medicine and cosmetics including hair care.
tech: Harvesting, drying, pulping, grinding, sorting and hand-milling kernels, then mixing with warm water
mat: Argan fruit and kernels
ctr: Women's cooperatives in the Arganeraie reserve
auth: Cooperative-made oil from the Moroccan reserve; very cheap 'pure argan' is suspect given the labour-intensive yield

d: Cleaning the teeth with a chewed twig: the miswak of Salvadora persica in the Islamic world, neem datun in India and chew sticks across Africa.
tech: The end of a fresh twig is chewed until its fibres splay into a brush; used before prayer in Islamic practice.
mat: Salvadora persica (arak, 'toothbrush tree'); neem; banyan and other local trees
auth: True miswak is cut from Salvadora persica; other woods are sold as generic chew sticks.

r: Aleppo, Syria (also made in Turkey and Damascus by relocated makers)
d: Hand-made hot-process olive-oil soap with laurel-berry oil, cut, stamped and aged for months.
tech: three-day boil in in-ground vats, laurel oil added last, poured on the floor, trodden smooth, cut, hand-stamped and cured in stacked towers
mat: olive oil, laurel-berry oil, lye, water
auth: laurel and olive scent, no animal fat or colour; laurel oil above 16% rated higher; widely imitated

p: significant industry by the 14th century; UNESCO ICH (urgent safeguarding) 2024
d: Olive-oil soap tradition of Nablus, cut into cubes, stamped with a family or factory seal and dried in tall cones.
tech: cooking by Al Tabbeekha, spreading and setting, cutting by Al Bikar, hand-stamping by Al Khatimeh, drying in hollow stacked cones
mat: virgin olive oil, water, sodium hydroxide
auth: ivory colour, almost no scent, factory seal stamped on each cube

p: c. 1370 to present; name regulated by the Edict of Colbert 1688
d: Cauldron-made vegetable-oil soap sold in stamped blocks and cubes, used for body and laundry.
tech: Marseille process in cauldrons: mashing, salting-out, boiling and further steps over days
mat: olive oil or palm and coconut oils, lye, sea salt
auth: UPSM collective mark; hard homogenous soap in traditional geometric shapes, cauldron-made; no whimsical shapes

d: Yoruba-origin soap made from the ash of plant peels and bark mixed with plant oils.
tech: sun-dried plant matter burned to ash for alkali, then cooked with water and oils
mat: plantain skins, palm leaves, cocoa pods, shea bark, palm kernel and other plant oils
auth: dark, uneven colour from plant ash

p: Han dynasty classics (1st c. BCE onward); modern system standardised in the PRC from the 1950s
d: Chinese healing tradition whose ready-made products are sold as patent medicines; listed here for forms and registration only.
tech: Herbal formulas made into pills, powders, pastes, extract granules and external plasters
mat: Plant, animal, fungal and mineral materials
auth: Mainland products follow Chinese Pharmacopoeia Vol. 1 monographs; Hong Kong proprietary Chinese medicines carry a registration number HKC-XXXXX; Tong Ren Tang products are often counterfeited.

p: Classical texts from the first centuries CE; mineral preparations (rasashastra) after the 11th century
d: South Asian healing tradition whose preparations are mostly plant-based; listed here for forms and registration only.
tech: Herbal compounding; rasashastra adds metals and minerals after purification (shodhana)
mat: Mostly plants; also metals, minerals, oils and fats
ctr: Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences
auth: Indian products must state metallic content; voluntary Ayush Standard Mark (Schedule T GMP) and Ayush Premium Mark (WHO GMP) run by the Quality Council of India since 2009.

p: Chinese medicine arrived in the 6th century; extract granules from the 1920s; NHI reimbursement from 1967
d: Japanese adaptation of Chinese herbal medicine using fixed formulas in standard proportions; listed here for forms and registration only.
tech: Fixed formulas made into dried decoction extract granules
mat: Crude herbal drugs listed in the Japanese Pharmacopoeia
ctr: Keio University Center for Kampo Medicine
auth: 148 formula extracts approved by Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, each with the same ingredients whichever maker.

r: South and Central Asia, chiefly India and Pakistan
p: Greco-Arabic, from Avicenna's Canon of Medicine; in India from the 12th century
d: Greco-Arabic humoral healing tradition practised in South Asia; listed here for forms and registration only.
tech: Herbal medicines compounded by hakims, with regimental therapies
mat: Herbs and minerals
ctr: Central Council for Research in Unani Medicine
auth: Regulated in India under the Ministry of Ayush and in Pakistan by the National Council for Tibb; Indian Unani products can carry the voluntary Ayush Mark.

d: Hydro-distillation of flowers, herbs and baked earth into a sandalwood base in copper stills; Kannauj perfumes hold a GI tag (2014).
tech: deg (copper still) sealed with clay, bamboo pipe to a bhapka of sandalwood oil, wood and cow-dung fire, repeated charges
mat: damask rose, jasmine, vetiver, kewra, baked clay, spices; sandalwood oil or liquid paraffin
auth: Kannauj GI tag; sandalwood rather than paraffin base; no alcohol; maker's distillery named

d: Wearing of dehn al oud, Taif rose oil, musk and blended mukhallat oils, traded by family houses in Gulf souqs.
tech: agarwood oil distillation; copper-pot distillation of Taif rose sold by the tola; blending into mukhallat
mat: agarwood (Aquilaria), Taif damask rose, white musk, amber, saffron
auth: origin and wood species stated; wild vs cultivated agarwood; natural oud oil yields are tiny, so cheap 'pure' oils are suspect
